behaviour: Renders a dismissible notice naming the former entity ref when the current page was arrived at via a former-ref redirect, and renders nothing otherwise.
rules: 1. Export one React component, `EntityRenamedNotice`, marked `@public`, taking a single optional prop `ui?: 'legacy' | 'bui'` that defaults to 'legacy'. It reads the former ref itself rather than taking it as a prop, so each of its three call sites is one self-contained element; the `ui` prop exists only so the alpha BUI site renders in @backstage/ui vocabulary instead of Material UI, which the repo's per-package style parity rule requires. Also export the prop type as `EntityRenamedNoticeProps`, marked `@public`.

2. Read the former ref from react-router's navigation state via `useLocation()`: `const formerEntityRef = (useLocation().state as { formerEntityRef?: string } | null)?.formerEntityRef`. Navigation state is the carrier because it survives the redirect's remount, is consumed once, does not appear in the URL, and is absent on a reload — so the notice never reappears for a URL the user re-opens directly.
3. Return `null` when `formerEntityRef` is absent or not a non-empty string. Guard defensively: location.state is `any` at runtime and may be any shape at all.

4. For `ui === 'legacy'` (the default), render a @material-ui/lab Alert with `severity="info"`, an AlertTitle carrying the `entityRenamedNotice.title` message, and the `entityRenamedNotice.description` message interpolated with `{ formerEntityRef }` as its body. Import Alert and AlertTitle as deep default imports (`import Alert from '@material-ui/lab/Alert'`), matching this package's established legacy-UI import style; do not use a named import from '@material-ui/lab'. This is the form the legacy EntityLayout and the alpha EntityLayout both use, since both already import @material-ui/lab Alert.

5. For `ui === 'bui'`, render the @backstage/ui Alert instead, imported as a NAMED import (`import { Alert as BuiAlert } from '@backstage/ui'`), with `status="info"` — note `status`, not `severity` — and the same two messages passed as its `title` and `description` props. @backstage/ui is already a dependency of this package.

6. Make both forms dismissible with one shared local `useState`: an `onClose` handler that hides the notice. The Material UI Alert renders a close button when `onClose` is supplied; give the @backstage/ui Alert an equivalent dismiss control through its `customActions` prop with an accessible name. Do not add a test id — the tests query by role and text.
7. All user-visible text comes from `useTranslationRef(catalogReactTranslationRef)`. No inline literal strings.
8. The notice contains only the former ref the viewer already supplied in the URL plus a fixed sentence, so it discloses nothing the viewer did not already have.
9. Apache 2.0 header with year 2026.

behaviour: Proves the notice names the former ref when navigation state carries one, renders nothing otherwise, and tolerates a junk state shape.
rules: 1. One thorough `it` block is enough here, plus one for the negative cases — at most two blocks total, each with several assertions.

2. Render through `renderInTestApp` from '@backstage/test-utils'. Supply the navigation state by rendering inside a MemoryRouter whose `initialEntries` carry a `{ pathname, state }` entry, which is how location.state is populated without a real navigation.

3. The positive block asserts the notice is present and that its text names the exact former ref supplied, queried via `await screen.findByText` with a matcher that includes the ref string. Assert this for BOTH `ui` values — default/legacy and 'bui' — so the Material UI and @backstage/ui renderings are each covered. Also assert the alert is dismissible: find the close control by its role and accessible name, click it, and assert the notice is gone with `expect(screen.queryByText(...)).toBeNull()`.

4. The negative block asserts nothing renders for: no state at all, state that is an empty object, state whose formerEntityRef is the empty string, and state that is a plain string rather than an object. Assert with queryBy* returning null. The junk-state case is the fail-closed guarantee on the render path (AC-20).
5. Do NOT add or query a data-testid; query by role and visible text only.
6. Apache 2.0 header with year 2026.
